examples.title: Sage arithmetic semantics
examples.note: The caret is exponentiation and integer division remains exact in Sage mode.

examples.title: Switch one cell to Python semantics
examples.note: The polyglot kernel preserves ordinary Python operators inside a %%python cell.

examples.title: Exact integer arithmetic
examples.code:
n = factorial(50)
(len(str(n)), gcd(n, 2026), factor(2026))
examples.note: Integers are arbitrary precision and participate in native factorization.

examples.title: Rational arithmetic stays exact
examples.code:
q = 22/7
(q, q.numerator(), q.denominator(), q^2)

examples.title: Arithmetic in a prime field
examples.code:
F = GF(101)
a = F(7)
(a^100, a.multiplicative_order(), (a + 5)/(a - 5))

examples.title: Factor an exact polynomial
examples.code:
R.<x> = QQ[]
f = x^8 - 1
(f.factor(), f(2))

examples.title: Multivariate polynomial rings
examples.code:
R.<x,y> = QQ[]
f = (x + y)^3
(f, f + x*y)

examples.title: A Gröbner basis in Macaulay2 syntax
examples.note: This uses the experimental Macaulay2 frontend and shared Sage.js polynomial objects.

examples.title: Exact matrix invariants
examples.code:
A = matrix(QQ, [[1,2,3], [0,1,4], [5,6,0]])
(A.det(), A.rank(), A.charpoly(), A.inverse())

examples.title: An exact right kernel
examples.code:
A = matrix(GF(2), [[1,1,0,1], [0,1,1,1]])
K = A.right_kernel()
(K.dimension(), K.basis())

examples.title: Isomorphism and automorphisms of the Petersen graph
examples.code:
G = graphs.PetersenGraph()
H = G.relabel({i:(7*i)%10 for i in range(10)}, inplace=False)
(G.order(), G.size(), G.girth(), G.is_isomorphic(H), G.automorphism_group().order(), G.chromatic_number())
examples.note: Packaged builds dispatch boolean isomorphism among native tiny-graph, Bliss, and VF2 kernels, and use Bliss for canonical labels and compact automorphism generators; certificates and unsupported cases retain the readable exact fallback.

examples.title: Query every small unlabeled graph
examples.code:
D = GraphDatabase()
regular = D.graphs(num_vertices=4, regular=True)
(D.count(), D.count(num_vertices=7), [G.degree_sequence() for G in regular])
examples.note: The bundled SQLite database contains every unlabeled graph on one through seven vertices.

examples.title: Interactive graph visualization
examples.code:
G = graphs.PetersenGraph()
G.show(interactive=True, vertex_color='#377eb8', vertex_size=30)
examples.expected: GraphPlot object for Petersen graph: Graph on 10 vertices
examples.note: Plotly remains the default; interactive=True selects a self-contained SVG whose vertices can be dragged with a mouse or touch in JupyterLab and CoCalc.

examples.title: Exact arithmetic in a number field
examples.code:
R.<x> = QQ[]
K.<a> = NumberField(x^4 + 1)
(a^4, a^8, (a+1)*(a-1), 1/(a+1), a.multiplicative_order())

examples.title: A quadratic class group
examples.code:
R.<x> = QQ[]
K.<a> = NumberField(x^2 + 17)
C = K.class_group()
(K.discriminant(), K.class_number(), C.invariants(), C.gen(), C.gen().order())

examples.title: Compute an integral basis
examples.code:
R.<x> = QQ[]
K.<a> = NumberField(x^3 + x^2 - 2*x + 8)
O = K.maximal_order()
(O.basis(), O.discriminant(), O.is_maximal())

examples.title: Exact ideal lattices
examples.code:
R.<x> = QQ[]
K.<a> = NumberField(x^3+x^2-2*x+8)
O = K.maximal_order()
I = O.ideal([2,a])
(I.gens_reduced(), I.norm(), (I^2).gens_reduced(), (I^2).norm(), a in I, 1 in I)

examples.title: Identify a quartic Galois group
examples.code:
R.<x> = QQ[]
G = NumberField(x^4 - x + 1, 'a').galois_group()
(G.transitive_label(), G.order(), G.is_galois(), G.is_abelian())

examples.title: Count primes without enumerating them
examples.code: prime_pi(10^12)

examples.title: Primality and factorization
examples.code:
n = 2^127 - 1
(is_prime(n), factor(2^32 - 1), next_prime(10^6))

examples.title: A Dirichlet character
examples.code:
G = DirichletGroup(21)
chi = G.1
(chi.conductor(), chi.modulus(), chi.order(), chi(19), chi(40))

examples.title: Generalized Bernoulli numbers
examples.code:
chi = DirichletGroup(5).0
[chi.bernoulli(k) for k in range(6)]

examples.title: Elliptic-curve point arithmetic
examples.code:
E = EllipticCurve([0,0,1,-1,0])
P = E([0,0])
(P, 2*P, 10*P, E.conductor(), E.j_invariant())

examples.title: Wild 2-adic local data
examples.code:
E = EllipticCurve([0,-2,0,-10,-8])
d = E.local_data(2)
(d.discriminant_valuation(), d.conductor_valuation(), str(d.kodaira_symbol()), d.tamagawa_number())

examples.title: Global conductor and reduction data
examples.code:
E = EllipticCurve([0,-2,0,9,8])
(E.global_minimal_model().ainvs(), E.minimal_discriminant(), E.conductor(), E.bad_primes(), E.tamagawa_numbers())

examples.title: Construct a Vélu isogeny
examples.code:
E = EllipticCurve([1,0,1,-171,-874])
P = E([15,-8])
phi = E.isogeny(P)
(phi.degree(), phi.codomain().ainvs(), phi(P).is_zero(), phi.kernel_polynomial())

examples.title: A Hecke operator on modular symbols
examples.code:
M = ModularSymbols(11)
(M.dimension(), M.weight(), M.T(2).matrix(), M.T(6).matrix() == M.T(2).matrix()*M.T(3).matrix())

examples.title: A cuspidal q-expansion
examples.code:
S = ModularSymbols(Gamma1(11), 2).cuspidal_submodule()
(S.dimension(), S.q_expansion_basis(10))

examples.title: Differentiate, integrate, and take a limit
examples.code:
f = sin(x^2)
(f.derivative(x), integral(x^2, x, 0, 1), limit(sin(2*x)/tan(3*x), x=0))

examples.title: A logarithmic definite integral
examples.code: integral(log(x)*x, (x, 2, 10))

examples.title: Adaptive quadrature with an error estimate
examples.code:
value, error = numerical_integral(exp(x^2), 1, 2)
(abs(value - 14.989976019600048) < 1e-12, error < 1e-10)

examples.title: NumPy arrays in Python mode
examples.code:
import numpy as np
A = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
(A.shape, A.sum(), A @ A)

examples.title: Compose interactive 2D graphics
examples.code:
g = line([(0, 0), (1, 1)], color='red', thickness=2)
g += point((0, 1), color='black', size=12)
(g, len(g), g.xmin(), g.xmax())
examples.note: In Jupyter the graphics object also produces an interactive Plotly display.

examples.title: Compose solids with an equal aspect ratio
examples.code:
G = tetrahedron((0,-3.5,0), color='blue')
G += cube((0,-2,0), color=(.25,0,.5))
G += octahedron(color='red') + dodecahedron((0,2,0), color='orange')
G += icosahedron(center=(0,4,0), color='yellow')
G.show(aspect_ratio=[1,1,1])
examples.note: The rich result uses Plotly's data aspect mode.

examples.title: Query an in-memory SQLite database
examples.code:
import sqlite3
db = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
db.execute('create table items(id integer primary key, name text)')
db.executemany('insert into items(name) values (?)', [('alpha',), ('beta',), ('gamma',)])
rows = db.execute('select id, name from items where id >= ? order by id', (2,)).fetchall()
db.close()
rows
